market_summary: September payrolls rose just 29,000 against 84,000-89,000 expected, unemployment rose to 4.2%, and July and August were revised down by a combined 60,000. The 10-year fell to about 5.20%, the dollar index lost 0.4%, and October hike odds fell to about 17%. At 10:30 ET the S&P 500 was +1.0%, Nasdaq +1.7% at a record intraday, Dow +0.5%, SOX +3.3%, VIX 15.5; the S&P is flat on the week. Asia closed mixed: ASX 200 +0.8%, Nikkei -0.9%, Hang Seng -2.6%, its worst session since March; Stoxx 600 +0.9% at midday. Brent fell about 3% to $99 and WTI 4% to $89 as Europe discussed releasing 50m barrels of diesel and 50m of crude. Next: OPEC+ Sunday Oct 4 (expected to hold November targets); Sydney clocks go to AEDT at 02:00 Sunday; ISM services Tue 01:00 AEDT; Marvell investor day Oct 6; Samsung and TSMC September revenue Oct 8; US CPI Oct 14.

AMZN.reason: Up about 1.6% in the first hour, outperforming a rising market on lower yields and the data center community pledge. The reported chip-financing idea is a balance-sheet detail, not a change to the thesis.

AXOS.reason: Up about 1.1% on lower yields with no company news. Next earnings are due October 29, so nothing to act on before then.

BABA.reason: Down 0.9% while the US group rose, after the Hang Seng fell 2.6% on the US yield surge. Lead-plaintiff deadline for the class action is Oct 5 and an executive sale is on the tape, so wait for yields and China policy to settle.

ENPH.reason: Up about 2.8% with rates and tech, but recent target cuts from Citi, Jefferies and Goldman and falling revenue keep this a watch until residential demand shows up.

FIGR.reason: Up about 4% after a sharp slide earlier in the week. Softer rates help its home equity lending model, but there is no company news, so no change.

GOOGL.reason: Up 1.8% on the day with no new negative news; the Gemini 4 Argon launch and the space-compute plans are still working through. A lower-yield tape helps long-duration growth, so the add stands.

LDI.reason: Up about 4.4% on the rates bounce, but it is still a sub-dollar stock with losses, an NYSE price-compliance notice and a Sell consensus. Use the strength to trim.

META.reason: Up 0.8%, lagging the other mega-caps after a 27% September. The New Mexico penalty claim is still unresolved, so hold rather than chase.

MRVL.reason: Up 2.9% on the day, among the stronger names in the group, with Investor Day on Oct 6 as the next catalyst. Hold through the event; one analyst note flags margin pressure from custom silicon.

MU.reason: Flat (down 0.1%) while the group rallied, so the record quarter is still not being rewarded on the tape. The YMTC suit is a minor IP item; nothing here changes the thesis.

NFLX.reason: Down about 0.7% while the market rallies, after a 14% drop in September on the co-CEO's slower-growth comments. Nothing new Friday; wait for Q3 earnings.

NVDA.reason: Up 2.8% on the day after Morgan Stanley reinstated it as top semiconductor pick and the weak jobs print cut October rate-hike odds. Already ahead of Thursday's close, so no reason to add into the move.

RKT.reason: Up about 2.8%, lagging the rally. The 10-year yield barely moved from Thursday's close, so mortgage rates are still near multi-year highs. Watch for a sustained yield decline.

TSM.reason: Up 2.3% on the day ahead of Q3 results on Oct 15, with the company guiding revenue in a tight range and Taiwan pledging support for local expansion. Keep adding on the weak-yield backdrop.

STRIPE.reason: No closed round or tender reported since the last run. A Benzinga item cites a private-market valuation estimate well above the mark, but it is not a closed deal and the article body could not be opened, so the mark is unchanged.

OPENAI.reason: No new closed round or tender since the last run. SoftBank finished its final tranche on Thursday; reported talks for a further $30 billion raise remain talks only, so the mark is unchanged.

headlines: US payrolls rose only 29,000 against 85,000 expected and unemployment hit 4.2%; October Fed hike odds fell to about 17%.
S&P 500 +1.0% and Nasdaq +1.7% at 10:30 ET Friday, a record intraday; SOX +3.3% and the 10-year down to 5.20%.
Tesla delivered 486,532 cars against 462,000 expected, shares +5.6%, but storage missed. Nvidia +2.8%, Marvell +2.9%, TSMC +2.3%.
Watchlist: BYD and Teradyne cut to watch. BYD fell 2.3% in Hong Kong after JPMorgan's downgrade; Teradyne is at its consensus target.
Broadcom is reportedly lining up $60B of debt for Anthropic's chips; Anthropic's IPO banks named, marketing from the week of Nov 9.
Weekend: OPEC+ meets Sunday; clocks go to AEDT. Brent fell 3% to about $99 on talk of Europe releasing diesel and crude.
